subject.title: fix(sessions): prevent disappearing usage and stalled cron cleanup

question: Should this protected session-state repair proceed after a current-main merge refresh and explicit confirmation of its persisted-state concurrency semantics?
rationale: The `maintainer` label requires explicit human handling, and the patch changes cleanup behavior for persisted agent session state where tests alone do not establish the operational concurrency contract.

options.title: Review and land after refresh
options.body: Rebase or refresh against current main, verify the required checks, and have the session-state owner confirm the conditional-delete and reaper-target semantics.

options.title: Request stronger runtime evidence first
options.body: Ask for a redacted terminal transcript or runtime log that demonstrates a refresh surviving cleanup and an immediate sweep after retention is re-enabled.

options.title: Pause for storage-contract redesign
options.body: Pause only if maintainers conclude the current snapshot-and-conditional-delete pattern does not match the canonical SQLite lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Review and land after refresh
recommendation.body: Rebase or refresh against current main, verify the required checks, and have the session-state owner confirm the conditional-delete and reaper-target semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The current PR commit is the only direct available ownership signal for these two session-state paths.
